chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'When you encounter a wild beast, say: I seek Refuge with the Lord of Daniel and the Pit, from the evil of every ferocious lion.'

key_terms.أَسَدٍ مُسْتَأْسِدٍ: Ferocious lion / lion in its natural state of ferocity
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْجُبِّ: The Pit (referring to the lions' den)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for protection from wild animals mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records a specific supplication taught by Imam Ali (AS) for protection against wild beasts, invoking the 'Lord of Daniel and the Pit.' It draws directly on the Quranic narrative of Prophet Daniel’s (Danyal) miraculous deliverance from lions, serving as a spiritual anchor for believers seeking divine safeguarding in times of danger. The reference to 'the Pit' (Al-Jubb) highlights the specific location of Daniel’s confinement, emphasizing God’s power to preserve His prophets even in the most perilous circumstances.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you come across a predatory wild animal, so say,
‘I seek Refuge with the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of Daniel and the Pit, from the evil of every ferocious lion’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘

If you come face to face with a beast say, ‘I seek protection with the Lord of Daniel and the well against the evil of all powerful lions.” Note: Daniel was thrown in a well with wild beasts but they did not harm him.
